--- title: "Minimal pairs (perception)" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_PERCEP_PARES_MINIMOS" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_PERCEP_PARES_MINIMOS`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Pares mínimos (percepción)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_PERCEP_PARES_MINIMOS.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Minimal pairs (perception), from age 4 to 7 (3,422 administrations in 5 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .23. AUC .45–.62 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2129 | | Battery | DIS-ESP | | Format | auditory stimuli | | Items | — | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | En esta prueba, se presentan de forma auditiva uno por uno 15 pares de sílabas. Las dos sílabas de cada par podrán ser iguales o diferentes. *(Spanish)* | ## Theoretical framework The **categorical perception** tasks (Serniclaes battery) use synthetic syllables ranging from BA to PA in voicing steps. In identification, the child says which syllable they hear; in discrimination, whether two syllables are the same or different. **Minimal pairs** ask the child to decide whether two real syllables are the same or different. They measure the precision of phonemic categories, the basis of letter–sound correspondences. **Phonological fluency** (saying, in 30 seconds, words that begin with a given phoneme) measures something else: lexical access from a sound and executive control. **What the evidence says:** - **Dyslexia shows a categorical perception deficit, clearer in discrimination.** A meta-analysis confirms the deficit compared with children of the same age and with younger readers at the same level. The effect is larger in discrimination than in identification [@noordenbos2015meta]. - **In Spanish, what fails is the boundary between categories.** In 204 Spanish children, those with dyslexia discriminated pairs that cross the phonemic boundary worse and some within-category differences better (allophonic perception) [@serniclaes2021allophonic]. That is why the total of correct responses mixes two effects of opposite sign. - **Its predictive value is modest and not entirely phonological.** In 237 children, perception at age 5½ predicted reading a year later without going through phonemic awareness. These tasks also capture decision making [@snowling2019speech]. In another study, its effect on decoding disappeared when phonological processing was controlled [@mcbridechang1997growth]. The evidence is therefore contradictory. - **Phonological fluency reflects access, not representations.** In 66 Greek children with dyslexia or developmental language disorder, word production was lower, but the size of clusters of related words was the same as in 83 controls [@mengisidou2019fluency]. **What our data show.** - **Categorical perception.** Discrimination does not predict persistent difficulty (AUC .39–.53) and identification barely does (.51–.63). This is to be expected if the total of correct responses is scored: the identification slope and between- and within-category discrimination should be computed from the item-by-item responses. - **Minimal pairs.** Low stability (ρ = .07–.39) and AUC from .45 to .69, better from age 5. Against Woodcock-Muñoz, .63–.66 at ages 6–7. - **Phonological fluency.** A single session at age 5 (793 children, almost all from Preleo schools): AUC of .68 against persistent difficulty and of .59–.62 against low comprehension. Internal consistency from item-level responses is missing. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2012| 5.2| 6.1| 279| 0.35| 0.39| | 2013| 4.1| 6.1| 314| 0.06| 0.07| ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (4.1, r = .20); Phonological awareness (5.1, r = .26); Letter knowledge (5.2, r = .26); Phonological awareness (6.1, r = .33); Word and text reading (7.2, r = .24). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .45–.62. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .50–.57. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_PERCEP_PARES_MINIMOS_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .41–.66 (3 time points; 143–254 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|----------:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.1| 568| 2013| 4.0| 4| 5| 6| 8| 9| 11| | 5.1| 347| 2014| 3.0| 4| 5| 6| 8| 10| 12| | 5.2| 319| 2012| 4.0| 5| 6| 7| 9| 11| 12| | 6.1| 726| 2012, 2013| 5.0| 6| 7| 7| 10| 12| 13| | 7.2| 253| 2010| 6.6| 7| 8| 9| 11| 12| 14| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_PERCEP_PARES_MINIMOS_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.1| 906| 0.057| 0.084| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.1| 1,047| 0.133| 0.032| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.1| 1,049| 0.088| 0.004| |School (ICC) | 4.1| 1,050| 0.101| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 335| 0.087| 0.110| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 312| 0.108| 0.344| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 334| 0.021| 0.703| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 347| 0.257| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 296| -0.017| 0.767| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 320| 0.121| 0.280| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 316| 0.092| 0.102| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 322| 0.182| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 884| 0.066| 0.050| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 881| 0.014| 0.839| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 878| 0.034| 0.308| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 890| 0.139| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.2| 745| 0.165| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.2| 809| 0.062| 0.382| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.2| 808| 0.041| 0.248| |School (ICC) | 7.2| 813| 0.128| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Minimal pairs (perception)” (code 2129; DIS-ESP battery) assesses phonological discrimination. Stimuli are presented auditorily and the child responds by selecting on the screen. The time limit is 90 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 7 sessions, from 4 to 7 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 8 months) was ρ = .39. Stability across time points was ρ = .07–.39. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .50–.57. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
